passage: Two poets each revised a sonnet they had written in youth. The first cut nearly a third of its lines, stripping out ornament she had come to distrust, and left a poem shorter but recognizably the same. The second kept every line and changed almost no words; instead he reordered the stanzas so that the poem ended where it had once begun, turning a lament into something closer to a resolution. The second poet, in other words, ______ the poem without trimming it.
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: By reordering the stanzas so the poem ended where it once began and moved toward resolution, the second poet changed where the poem goes: he "redirected" it. "Personalized" fails because nothing in the revision makes the poem more about the poet; it changes the poem’s direction. "Republished" fails because the passage describes a change to the poem’s structure, not a new appearance in print, and "padded" fails because the change was a reordering of existing stanzas rather than added filler.

deletion_test.kept_sentence: The second poet, in other words, ______ the poem without trimming it.
deletion_test.why: alone, any treatment that leaves the length intact fits: redirecting, personalizing, republishing and padding all avoid trimming; only the description of the second revision (reordered stanzas, lament turned to resolution) and the contrast with the first poet decide it
